content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss validation, authorization, session, and secret-handling weaknesses. This skill gives developers a practical defensive checklist for safer web changes.
actual_capabilities: Review server-side input validation and normalization requirements.
Identify unsafe output sinks and recommend context-specific encoding.
Check authorization, session rotation, password hashing, and token comparison practices.
Review CSRF controls, cookie attributes, CORS settings, and security headers.
Flag secret exposure, unsafe logging, open redirects, SSRF risks, and dependency weaknesses.
Produce a focused security review checklist for web application changes.
limitations: It provides guidance and review prompts, not automated vulnerability scanning.
It cannot verify runtime configuration, deployed headers, or infrastructure controls.
Recommendations require framework-specific implementation and testing.
It does not replace an independent penetration test or security audit.

use_cases.title: Review a Web Feature
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to examine validation, output encoding, authorization, sessions, and secrets before merging a feature.

use_cases.title: Assess an API Endpoint
use_cases.description: Check an endpoint for injection, CSRF, object-level authorization, redirect, SSRF, and sensitive logging risks.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Security Review
use_cases.description: Turn common application-security controls into a structured review agenda for a team or release.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this web change for input validation, output encoding, authorization, sessions, CSRF, and secret-handling issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small web change

prompt_templates.title: Review an API Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this API route. Identify trust boundaries, validation gaps, injection risks, authorization failures, and unsafe response handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this authentication flow for password storage, session rotation, token lifetime, logout invalidation, and constant-time comparisons.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a prioritized remediation plan from this security review. Include evidence, impact, recommended controls, tests, and residual risk.

output_examples.input: Review a login endpoint that accepts credentials and creates a session cookie.
output: Use a maintained password hashing library.
Rotate the session after login and set Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite attributes.
Add rate limiting and tests for failed authorization.

output_examples.input: Assess a profile page that renders a user biography and accepts a redirect parameter.
output_examples.output: Encode biography content for its output context, sanitize approved rich text, and allow redirects only to trusted destinations.

best_practices: Validate and normalize untrusted input at the server boundary.
Use framework protections and vetted libraries before custom security code.
Test authorization, error paths, secure headers, logging, and secret handling.
anti_patterns: Trusting client-side validation or identifiers for authorization.
Concatenating untrusted input into queries, commands, HTML, or URLs.
Storing plaintext passwords or logging secrets, tokens, and full authorization headers.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews common web security boundaries, including validation, encoding, authorization, sessions, secrets, transport, and dependencies.

faq.question: Does it scan my application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance for reviewing code and design decisions.

faq.question: Can it review authentication flows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers password hashing, session lifecycle, token handling, authorization, and constant-time comparisons.

faq.question: Does it replace penetration testing?
faq.answer: No. Use it for development reviews, then obtain testing appropriate to your application and threat model.

faq.question: Which applications benefit most?
faq.answer: Web applications, APIs, and services that process user input, sessions, credentials, or sensitive data.

faq.question: How should teams use the recommendations?
faq.answer: Apply them during design and code review, then verify controls with targeted tests and deployment checks.
